answer: A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases hence burns capital on every one it does not finish. Because the jetty deposit is held in the fable escrow, the sonnet audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 69 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. A farm of 211 pays that 23 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
